Eccentric

ik-SEN-trik — literally 'off-center'; an eccentric person just doesn't orbit the same way everyone else does. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Eccentric is unconventional and a little strange, especially in behavior or appearance.

The eccentric millionaire kept a pet llama in his living room and answered his front door dressed as a pirate.

Worked Example

A brilliant chemistry teacher insists on wearing a different colored lab coat every day of the week, keeps a collection of over two hundred rubber ducks on his desk, and always ends class by singing the periodic table instead of just reciting it.

Being delightfully odd and unconventional in a harmless way is exactly what eccentric means. Unlike 'crazy,' which can suggest something is wrong, eccentric usually has a fond, admiring tone about someone's quirks.

How Eccentric Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

quirky

quirky: having odd or unusual habits or traits

unconventional

unconventional: not following what is normal or expected

peculiar

peculiar: strange or unusual

Antonyms

conventional

conventional: following what is normal or expected

ordinary

ordinary: not unusual or special; normal

How Strong Is It? — quirky → eccentric → bizarre

quirky vs. eccentric

quirky vs. eccentric: Quirky is a lighter, more affectionate word than eccentric — quirky often describes small, charming habits, while eccentric can describe a whole unconventional lifestyle or personality.

bizarre vs. eccentric

bizarre vs. eccentric: Bizarre can feel more extreme than eccentric: eccentric usually has a fond, harmless tone, but bizarre suggests something genuinely strange or hard to explain.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ec- (ek-)

prefix — ec- (ek-): out of (Greek)

root — -centr-

root — -centr-: center (Greek (kentron))

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the nature of (Greek (-ikos))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek ek- ('out of') plus kentron ('center') plus the adjective ending -ic ('having the nature of') builds 'off-center.' Someone eccentric literally doesn't orbit the same conventional path as everyone else.
